urls.content:
# [FR]: Eliminate dead zones (spacing) between tab click targets

- State: open
- Author: jwadow
- Created: 2026-04-22T04:22:20Z
- Updated: 2026-04-22T08:02:49Z
- Repository: imputnet/helium
- Number: #1417

## Labels

- feat
- pending

---

### Description

Remove the 3px unclickable gaps between tabs to improve navigation and closing speed

### Who's implementing?

- [ ] I'm willing to implement this feature myself

### The problem

There is a small spacing (roughly 3px depending on resolution) between individual tabs. When multiple tabs are open and shrunk to icon size, these gaps create "dead zones". This leads to missed clicks when switching tabs rapidly or batch-closing them via middle-click. In browsers like Brave, these zones are unified, allowing for a seamless interaction area. Currently, these gaps serve no functional purpose and hinder UX flow on standard resolutions like 1080p

 

### Possible solutions

Expand the interactive hitboxes (click targets) of the tabs so they are flush against each other. The visual spacing between tab elements can remain the same for aesthetic clarity, but the underlying "invisible" click zone should be continuous

Actually, a 3px gap between tabs probably isn't the whole story since they have rounded corners at the top. at the top, the gap might even be more like 4-5px, but that's just a guess. either way, i'd suggest just going with fully square hitboxes that are flush against each other.

 

### Additional context

This is particularly noticeable on Full HD screens where the 3px gap is wide enough to register as a "miss" during fast mouse movement

### Description

Quickly preview links without opening a full tab

### Who's implementing?

- [ ] I'm willing to implement this feature myself

### The problem

When browsing in Helium, opening a link always means either navigating away from the current page or creating a full tab. A lot of the time I only want to quickly inspect the destination, confirm it is what I need, and then continue where I was. Using full tabs for that breaks browsing flow and creates unnecessary tab clutter.

### Possible solutions

Add a lightweight link preview mode that can open any link in a temporary preview instead of a full tab. It should be fast to trigger, easy to dismiss, and easy to promote into a normal tab if I decide to keep it open. A modifier-click and/or context menu action could be a good trigger.

### Additional context

The general idea is similar to Arc's Peek or Zen Browser's Glance: a quick, temporary way to inspect links without losing context. Helium does not need to copy either feature exactly, but a Helium-native version of that workflow would be very useful.

### Description

Integrate native, customizable Vim-like keybindings for core browser actions for keyboard-driven navigation

### Who's implementing?

- [ ] I'm willing to implement this feature myself

### The problem

Browser extensions like Vimium (I use Vimium C specifically) allow keyboard-driven navigation, but they are limited by the browser's extension APIs. Using them is sometimes inconsistent and a less fluid experience when they cannot control certain browser functions or operate on some internal pages (e.g., new tab pages, settings).

### Possible solutions

Helium could have native, customizable Vim-like keybindings for browser actions, which could work at the browser level without the above limitations. I feel this would make Helium great for people who are already used to a keyboard driven workflow across their apps.

My most frequently used key bindings which speed up using any browser are
- t to open new tab and focus url bar
- e and r to switch tabs left and right
- dd or x to close tab
- c to search selected text in new tab
- s to focus the url bar
- gi to focus input fields
- a to allow for passthrough for the keys even if no textbox is selected
- f to select links / focus area

These are active everywhere when no textbox is focused on the page and makes every browser feel even faster to use. I feel this could truly set this browser apart along with the already existing features.

### Description

Remove the 3px unclickable gaps between tabs to improve navigation and closing speed

### Who's implementing?

- [ ] I'm willing to implement this feature myself

### The problem

There is a small spacing (roughly 3px depending on resolution) between individual tabs. When multiple tabs are open and shrunk to icon size, these gaps create "dead zones". This leads to missed clicks when switching tabs rapidly or batch-closing them via middle-click. In browsers like Brave, these zones are unified, allowing for a seamless interaction area. Currently, these gaps serve no functional purpose and hinder UX flow on standard resolutions like 1080p

 

### Possible solutions

Expand the interactive hitboxes (click targets) of the tabs so they are flush against each other. The visual spacing between tab elements can remain the same for aesthetic clarity, but the underlying "invisible" click zone should be continuous

Actually, a 3px gap between tabs probably isn't the whole story since they have rounded corners at the top. at the top, the gap might even be more like 4-5px, but that's just a guess. either way, i'd suggest just going with fully square hitboxes that are flush against each other.

 

### Additional context

This is particularly noticeable on Full HD screens where the 3px gap is wide enough to register as a "miss" during fast mouse movement

a new tab gets placed next to the focused tab instead of the end of the tab bar
